summary: Iter183 — Shipment AI scanner + waybill + extended item model. Backend: 8/8 tests in /app/backend/tests/test_iter183_scanner_waybill.py PASS against external URL (ISBN→Google Books, UPC→OpenFoodFacts, missing-signals→400, missing-token→401, extended item fields persist incl. parent_id stacking, admin & public waybill render with $40.98 / 1.20 kg totals, public waybill correctly requires X-Shipment-Edit-Token). Frontend: donor page at /donate/shipment/{token} loads, PIN login succeeds (badge ship-donor-editor-badge appears), 'Scan item' (ship-donor-open-scanner) and 'Waybill' (ship-donor-waybill) buttons both visible, scanner dialog (ship-donor-scanner-dialog) opens with dropzone + hidden file input + AI submit, file upload renders previews (ship-donor-scan-previews), Identify with AI button enables. No console errors. One real UX bug found in the Waybill button (see below).

ui_bugs.issue: Clicking the Waybill button (data-testid='ship-donor-waybill') calls window.open() with /api/public/shipments/{token}/waybill — but that endpoint requires the X-Shipment-Edit-Token header, which window.open() cannot send. Confirmed live: GET on that URL without the header returns 401. So the donor-page Waybill button currently leads to an Unauthorized page even after the user has logged in with the PIN. Backend test (test_public_waybill_requires_pin) is correct — the issue is on the frontend.

integration_issues.issue: Frontend uses window.open() but the public waybill API only accepts the edit token via header. Two acceptable fixes: (a) backend accepts ?edit_token=... query param fallback on /api/public/shipments/{token}/waybill, or (b) frontend fetches the HTML with header and opens a blob URL in a new tab.

action_items: Fix the donor-page Waybill button so the PIN-gated waybill actually opens. Recommended: backend accepts ?edit_token=... query param on GET /api/public/shipments/{token}/waybill (mirrors how some browsers handle attachments), OR frontend fetches HTML with X-Shipment-Edit-Token header and opens it as a blob: URL. Without this fix, Waybill button leads to 401 page.
Review request prose says donor URL is /donate/{token} — the actual mounted route is /donate/shipment/{token} (App.js line 131). Either update prose or add /donate/{token} alias.

Scanner 'Identify with AI' end-to-end (real Gemini/GPT vision) was not exercised in this run because we used a 1x1 dummy JPG. Backend ISBN/UPC paths are fully covered by pytest. If you want a full UI screenshot of the result panel (ship-donor-scan-result + container_type + pallet picker + parent picker + confirm), the easiest path is to seed an item via POST /api/shipments/{id}/items, then exercise the existing-item editor — the scanner result panel itself is straightforward React state.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Donor route is /donate/shipment/{token} NOT /donate/{token}. ISBN/UPC are query params on scan-item (?isbn=... or ?upc=...). Editor token header is X-Shipment-Edit-Token. Toast after PIN login takes ~2s; sleep 2.5s before clicking Scan item or it can intercept the click. Scan dialog appears as role='dialog' in a portal — query by [data-testid='ship-donor-scanner-dialog'] works via Playwright locator. Backend tests pass with BACKEND_URL=https://multi-tenant-scope.preview.emergentagent.com. The single open bug is the Waybill window.open header problem described above.
rca of the issue: Waybill 401: window.open() always issues a plain GET with only cookies — it cannot attach custom request headers like X-Shipment-Edit-Token. The backend route /api/public/shipments/{token}/waybill requires that header (correctly, by design). Reproduction: (1) create shipment + set PIN, (2) open /donate/shipment/{token}, (3) submit PIN, (4) click Waybill — browser opens new tab with 401 JSON. Mitigation: either accept ?edit_token=... query param on the public waybill endpoint (server.py public router) OR change frontend to fetch with header then open a blob URL.
